messages.author: c35d90904ba3a8a5
messages.subject: Shiny, knitr and dynamic reporting
parts:
I hope that with his topic an uncovered area will be more clearly defined. Lets say we have a shiny app with some ui.R (or www/index.html) and a server.R. Lets suppose that the shiny app has for simplicity two input textfields one for first name and one for last name of an individual. Consider that we have properly structured a .Rnw document that waits for some R to be injected. So the question is. How input$firstname and input$lastname would be passed in the .Rnw document so that knit2pdf() function will produce dynamically a report with each first name and last name that an individual types. And lastly , how the new download link will produced in server.R?

**i set this questions after i have written whatelse is marked under shiny and knitr

I think it is a very interesting part and i think that reactiveRnw() function should be a must have addition in next shiny release!

messages.subject: Re: Shiny, knitr and dynamic reporting
parts:
My gut not tested thoughts-
Before running the .Rnw, put the input$objects -> regularObjects, then use initialized regularObjects in the .Rnw
ie:
somewhere inside the server.r-
obj1 <- input$shiny1
obj2 <- input$shiny2
Sweave(myRNW.Rnw) # I haven't used knitR so I'm not sure if knit2pdf is the command that actually runs the .Rnw, so am just going with Sweave

somewhere inside the .Rnw-
if(obj1>obj2){
x=1
}else{
x=2

}

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny, knitr and dynamic reporting
parts:
Use downloadButton("report") in your ui.R, and on the server:

output$report <- downloadHandler(
  filename = "myreport.pdf",
  content = function(file) {
    knit2pdf("input.Rnw", file)
  },
  contentType = "application/pdf"
)

In your Rnw I *think* you should be able to simply refer to input$firstname and input$lastname directly.
